text:
maya: Heads-up — I'm opening a small docs PR to reconcile the 429 troubleshooting page with the new SDK retry behavior we shipped last week. Found a few places that still say 'client should retry after X' but our SDK now has built-in backoff + jitter.

samir: Nice. Link? I'll skim for any user-facing contradictions (esp. around rate-limit headers).

maya: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/472 — main changes are: clarify when a 429 is transient vs permanent, remove manual retry code examples in favor of SDK snippets, and add a note about context-length errors being surfaced as 400 vs truncated responses depending on model config.

alex: Quick question: we previously recommended reading Retry-After header for 429s. Do we keep that note or say "prefer SDK backoff"?

natalie: Prefer SDK backoff for most users, but keep a short section about "advanced" handling: reading Retry-After for strict rate-limit policies (enterprise/dedicated cases) and examples for servers that need to map to HTTP 503 for upstream.

maya: Agreed. I reworded the intro: "For typical integrations use Redwood SDKs which implement exponential backoff and jitter. If you manage raw HTTP calls or need strict SLA mapping, consult the Retry-After example below."

samir: For the SDK snippet, can we show both JS and Python minimal examples? Also include how to opt out of SDK retries if someone wants manual control.

maya: Added both. JS snippet:

```js
// SDK auto-retry enabled by default
import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
try {
  const r = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-3b', input: 'hello' });
  console.log(r.text);
} catch (e) {
  console.error('generation failed', e);
}
```

And a short note: to disable retries set retries: 0 in the client options.
\n\nalex: For the Python snippet please show how to read Retry-After if retries disabled. Something like:

```py
from redwood import Redwood
client = Redwood(api_key=os.getenv('RW_KEY'), retries=0)
resp = client.request(...)  # raises on 429
if resp.status_code == 429:
    retry_after = resp.headers.get('Retry-After')
    # fallback to a queue or user-facing 429
```

That should cover advanced cases.

docs-bot: CI check started for PR #472 — lint/docs linkcheck running :gear:

maya: Another thing: context-limit behavior. The runtime can either reject requests that exceed model context (400 with code CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE) or accept and truncate oldest tokens depending on deployment config. I added a small table but want wording exact: "By default Hosted returns a 400 (CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE). For Dedicated you may configure truncation; see admin guide."

natalie: Maybe phrase as: "Default behavior (Hosted): request is rejected with 400. Dedicated/Private: configurable — may truncate or reject; admins should document behavior in their contract." Keeps it short and precise.

samir: Also add a short migration note: "If you previously relied on silent truncation, test your flows after upgrading to latest SDK and runtime — you may start seeing 400s."

maya: Yep added migration checklist and a tiny test snippet that asserts for 400.

alex: Link fixes? There were a couple of old links to /guides/ratelimits — we moved to /troubleshooting/rate-limits. I updated and left redirects note.

maya: I also removed a confusing figure that displayed a retry loop. It made users think they should implement their own exponential backoff. Replaced with a single diagram showing "Client -> SDK backoff -> Redwood -> model".

ci-bot: docs linkcheck passed. lint passed. :white_check_mark:

maya: Great — I'll mark the PR ready for review. @samir @alex can you do a quick pass focusing on wording for Retry-After vs SDK? If possible ship today as it's blocking a customer migration. :pray:

samir: Will review in 30m. :eyes:

alex: On it. :+1:

natalie: Thanks Maya — can you also add a tiny note in the release notes? I can copy it into the migration guide.
maya: Done — added release-notes snippet at end of doc.

maya: One more tiny detail: updated the examples directory path in code blocks to `examples/rate-limits/` so relative links work. Double-check those files exist before merge.

samir: Confirmed examples exist in the branch. LGTM once wording tweaks are in.

maya: Thanks everyone — merging after reviews. Will follow up if customers report unexpected 400s so we can iterate on guidance. :shipit:
